newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ First releases coalition talks timetable.
newsitem.headline: NZ First releases coalition talks timetable.

text.p: Nationalist New Zealand First on Monday released the schedule for the fourth week of formal coalition talks.
In a statement NZ First spokesman Mike Booker said the party would hold talks with the caretaker National Party on Tuesday at 2 p.m., on Wednesday at 10 a.m. and on Thursday at 10 a.m.
NZ First will meet the main opposition Labour Party for talks at 5 p.m. on Tuesday, at 2 p.m. on Wednesday and at 2 p.m. on Thursday.
NZ First holds the balance of power after the inconclusive October 12 election and is running parallel talks with National and Labour over the shape of the next government.

Parliament must meet no later than December 13. A speaker will be elected on the first day parliament sits, but the leaders of the three parties to the talks have said a decision on the new government may not be reached by then.
